comparison: Perfect agreement on validation of simulation approach using dEGFR (C41-C47). Both evaluations confirm the simulations correctly reproduce experimental observations and validate the MD methodology.

Both address specific molecular interactions (C72-C80). OpenEval finds the sequence conservation analysis and identified interactions well-supported, while peer reviewers request more detailed interface analysis and consider the presented evidence insufficient.

Both evaluate dimerization arm and binding affinity differences (C82, C85-C91). OpenEval acknowledges speculation but considers observations reasonable; peer reviewers directly challenge the treatment as misleading and inadequate for addressing known affinity differences.

Both address evolutionary conservation claims (C6, C40, C92, C104). OpenEval finds convergent evidence across systems compelling; peer reviewers acknowledge importance but express concern that findings merely confirm Drosophila work without sufficient new mechanistic insights.

Both evaluate ligand-dependent stabilization findings (C5, C32, C59, C94). Strong agreement that simulations demonstrate stable heterodimers with single ligand, with peer reviewers highlighting this as an important finding.

Both address domain II conformation mechanism (C34-C36, C64-C65, C96-C97, C100-C101). Agreement that simulations demonstrate domain II conformation controls interface stability, though peer reviewers request more detailed interface analysis.
Both evaluate reproducibility of simulations (C112-C113). Strong agreement with peer reviewers explicitly praising the reproducibility across independent simulations of this large system.
OpenEval addresses Her3-Her2 heterodimer stability (C69-C70); peer result R2 includes C69 in broader heterodimer findings. Both support ligand-dependent stabilization in Her3-Her2 system.
Both address Her2 homodimer instability (C33, C60). Agreement that simulations show Her2 homodimer interface opens to produce gap, presented as validated result.

OpenEval evaluates 1-ligand EGFR homodimer model assumption (C51-C58); peer R4 addresses evolutionary conservation including structural similarity claims (C52-C53). Both express uncertainty about validation, though for different aspects.

OpenEval focuses on conformational transition and wedge mechanism (C96-C97, C100, C103); peer R5 includes these claims (C96-C97, C100) in broader mechanistic evaluation. Both support the domain II conformational mechanism.

OpenEval evaluates sequence identity justifying homology modeling (C50, C105-C107). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this methodological aspect was not explicitly assessed by peer reviewers.

Peer reviewers challenge characterization of Her3-Her2 heterodimers as 'particularly robust' (C67-C68), stating no evidence supports exceptional affinity. OpenEval does not have a corresponding evaluation of these specific claims.
